correctness.rationale: The induced-degree inequalities exactly classify each face, and the mixed-face counts sum to the stated polynomial. All maximal faces are either a whole shore or the 4-vertex pair-of-pairs simplex. A relative simplicial contiguity argument retracts the two-index subcomplex onto the complete shore graph; adjoining its full simplex yields a contractible union, and gluing the opposite simplex along its shore graph gives the suspension of \(K_n\) as an integral homotopy type. Independent exhaustive tests check 87,360 subsets and mod-two homology over orders 3–8; the infinite and integral assertions rely on proof, not finite sampling.

value.rationale: Dissociation/higher-independence complexes are a mathematically motivated topological model of induced maximum-degree-one vertex systems. For an entire canonical bipartite family, removal of a perfect matching from \(K_{n,n}\) raises homotopy dimension from a wedge of circles (known) to an explicitly quantified wedge of 2-spheres. Complete face and facet enumerators additionally give an unusual pure-only-at-four transition, with arbitrarily separated facet sizes as \(n\) increases; these are structural, independently meaningful refinements not contained in a maximum-cardinality theorem.
